stem: In a glomerular model, blood colloid-osmotic pressure is lowered while glomerular and capsular hydrostatic pressures remain fixed. A second investigator wants to restore the original net filtration pressure without changing the filtration coefficient. Which of the following paired observations and adjustments is appropriate?

options.text: GFR stays stable; maintain capsular pressure to preserve it
options.explanation: Net filtration pressure changes when one opposing pressure changes and the others remain fixed. Stable filtration cannot be assumed under the stated controlled conditions.
options.label: A
options.misconception: Assumes unchanged filtration when an opposing pressure changes and the other conditions remain fixed.

options.text: GFR initially rises; increase capsular pressure to offset it
options.explanation: Lower blood colloid-osmotic pressure removes opposition to filtration. Raising capsular pressure adds opposition back, permitting restoration of the original net driving pressure in this controlled model.
options.label: B
options.misconception: No misconception: reduced colloid-osmotic opposition raises filtration, and added capsular opposition can offset it.

options.text: GFR initially falls; increase capsular pressure to offset it
options.explanation: Lowering colloid-osmotic opposition initially increases rather than decreases filtration. Increasing capsular pressure would oppose the true change, but the stated initial response is incorrect.
options.label: C
options.misconception: Reverses the initial filtration response to a reduction in blood colloid-osmotic opposition.

options.text: GFR initially rises; decrease capsular pressure to offset it
options.explanation: The initial response is correct, but lowering another opposing pressure would increase the driving pressure further. Restoring the baseline requires adding opposition instead.
options.label: D
options.misconception: Attempts to offset reduced opposition by lowering another opposing pressure, which reinforces the initial change.

options.text: GFR initially falls; decrease capsular pressure to offset it
options.explanation: This starts with the wrong GFR direction. Lower blood colloid-osmotic pressure favors filtration, and reducing capsular pressure would reinforce rather than cancel that effect.
options.label: E
options.misconception: Reverses the initial filtration response and chooses a capsular adjustment that reinforces the true change.

context: Learning objective: Use opposing filtration forces to predict a response and identify a compensating experimental adjustment. Lower blood colloid-osmotic pressure removes opposition to filtration. Raising capsular pressure adds opposition back, permitting restoration of the original net driving pressure in this controlled model.
